output_json.patch_notes:
Ported the upstream Apache Sling fix for CVE-2024-23673 (fixed in org.apache.sling.servlets.resolver 2.11.0, this repo was at 2.10.0):

1. Added `public static boolean isInvalidPath(final String path)` to SlingServletResolver.java — walks the path segment-by-segment (split on '/') and rejects any segment longer than 2 characters that consists entirely of dots (e.g. "...", "...."), which bypass the existing ".." normalization/allow-list checks on some resource providers.
2. In `resolveServletInternal(...)`, call `isInvalidPath(scriptNameOrResourceType)` up front and bail out (return null, with a progress-tracker log entry) before any normalization/resolution happens — this is the sink reached from resource-type-derived paths and from the public `resolveServlet(Resource,String)` / `resolveServlet(ResourceResolver,String)` APIs (NamedScriptResourceCollector path), covering all the traced flows through ScriptResourceResolver/AbstractResourceCollector/ServletResource/ScriptResource.
3. In `SlingScriptResolverImpl.findScript(...)`, wrapped the existing absolute/relative resolution logic in the same `!isInvalidPath(name)` guard, closing the sibling call site that shares the same root cause.
4. Added `SlingServletResolverTest.java` with the upstream unit tests for `isInvalidPath` covering absolute/relative paths, leading/trailing/middle segments, and legitimate dotted names (e.g. "b.c.d.e.f") that must remain allowed.

No behavior change for legitimate paths (normal "..", single ".", or dots embedded in filenames like "foo.bar.js" continue to work); only segments that are purely 3+ dots are newly rejected.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the change is a narrow allow/deny check added before existing resolution logic, matches the official upstream patch verbatim, and the full existing test suite (166 tests) plus the new regression test pass with no failures. SpotBugs static analysis (run as part of `mvn package`) also reported zero findings. The only behavioral change is that resource-type/script-name path segments consisting solely of 3 or more dots are now rejected — this is intentionally the security fix and should not affect any legitimate resource type, script, or servlet path in real deployments.
output_json.summary: Fixed CVE-2024-23673 (CWE-22 path traversal) in Apache Sling Servlets Resolver. The two script/servlet resolution entry points — SlingServletResolver.resolveServletInternal(...) (used for resource-type-derived and directly-supplied script/servlet paths) and SlingScriptResolverImpl.findScript(...) — only guarded against ".." traversal via ResourceUtil.normalize() + isPathAllowed(), but did not reject path segments made entirely of 3+ dots (e.g. "...", "...."). Some resource providers/filesystems resolve such segments as parent-directory references, letting an attacker with write access to the repository craft a resource type or script name that escapes the configured executionPaths allow-list and gets treated as an executable script/servlet. Added a shared SlingServletResolver.isInvalidPath(String) check (path segment of >2 chars where every char is '.') and applied it at both entry points before any path is normalized/resolved, closing the shared root cause for all traced sink paths (ScriptResourceResolver -> AbstractResourceCollector.getResourceOrNull, ServletResourceProvider/ServletResource/ScriptResource path field, and SlingServletResolver.resolveServletInternal) as well as the SlingScriptResolverImpl sibling call site. This mirrors the official upstream fix shipped in org.apache.sling.servlets.resolver 2.11.0.
